verdict_text:
YES

The script drops blocks 2, 6, 10, 14, renumbers the survivors in original order to 0..11 exactly as the specification's mapping requires, passes the two non-block tensors through untouched, and writes a single `out/T1/model.safetensors`. Building a fresh output dict avoids the rename-collision hazard. The two assertions run before `save_file`, so a violation exits non-zero with nothing written: `layers == set(range(12))` enforces both "no block 12..15 remains" and "exactly 12 blocks", and `len(out) == 86` enforces the tensor count. The only unverifiable piece is the imported `_ckpt.load_checkpoint`, assumed to load the sharded directory into a plain name-to-tensor dict without altering values or dtypes.
